issues.legal_issue: A co-defendant who loses a legal benefit when a first appellate decree overturns a decree in which the co-defendant benefited is a person aggrieved and may maintain a second appeal against that decree.
material_facts: The appellant was a co-defendant who supported the plaintiff’s claim that the disputed property was joint family property and that the will was invalid.
The trial court decreed the suit, granting a benefit to the appellant.
The beneficiaries appealed, and the plaintiff settled with them; the first appellate court reversed the trial decree and dismissed the suit.
That reversal extinguished the benefit the appellant had obtained and adversely affected his legal rights.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was prejudicially affected by the first appellate decree and could maintain a second appeal against it. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s decision on maintainability and remitted the second appeal for decision on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 96 and 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 provide appeals from decrees but do not specify exhaustively who may appeal. A person whose legal right or interest is adversely affected by a decree is a person aggrieved and may appeal; a merely psychological or imaginary injury is insufficient. The Court relied on Jatan Kanwar Golcha v. Golcha Properties Private Ltd., State of Punjab v. Amar Singh, Baldev Singh v. Surinder Mohan Sharma, Banarsi v. Ram Phal, and Ayaaubkhan Noorkhan Pathan v. State of Maharashtra. It distinguished Ganga Bai v. Vijay Kumar, which concerned an appeal against a mere finding and predated the 1976 amendment to Order 41 Rule 22.

rule.if: second_appeal_proceeding and appellant_party_to_suit and appellant_benefited_from_trial_decree and appellate_reversal_extinguished_benefit and legal_right_adversely_affected

predicates.second_appeal_proceeding: The proceeding is a second appeal against a decree.
predicates.appellant_party_to_suit: The person seeking to appeal was a party to the suit.
predicates.appellant_benefited_from_trial_decree: The appellant supported a claim that the trial court accepted and benefited from the resulting decree.
predicates.appellate_reversal_extinguished_benefit: A first appellate court reversed the decree and thereby removed the benefit the appellant had obtained.
predicates.legal_right_adversely_affected: The reversal adversely affected a legal right or interest of the appellant.

issues.definition: When a party to a second appeal loses a benefit under a trial decree because it is reversed on appeal, and that reversal adversely affects the party’s legal right or interest, the second appeal is maintainable.
